current_activity: the division completes the capture of Nuremberg on 20 April, Hitler's birthday
notes: Event date: 20 April 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 18 p. 425: late on 19 April the 3d Division's 30th Infantry penetrated the medieval walls to enter the old town; before daylight the next morning the gauleiter directed a last counterattack, "the shrine of nazism fell, ironically, on 20 April, Hitler's birthday"; Wikipedia, Battle of Nuremberg (1945): on 20 April the 3d Infantry Division under Maj. Gen. John W. O'Daniel and the 45th Infantry Division laid siege to the old city and the city centre fell on that day). Event definition: the division completes the capture of the city; the 30th Infantry, a regiment of the division, is the unit named for the entry into the old town. Relationship: XV Corps unspecified_subordination (from 12 Mar 45 to 20 Apr 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 12 Mar 45, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 15 Sep 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier assigned relation to Seventh Army (CR0217) is closed at 17 February 1945 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. The earlier unspecified_subordination relation to VI Corps (CR0215) is closed at 14 December 1944 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Nuremberg, the old town standing for the objective. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Nuremberg. Event support: strong (the Green Book and Wikipedia agree on the day, the unit and the place). Location support: good (named city and old town).

current_activity: the division escorts the emissaries of Army Group G to Haar, near Munich, for the surrender of the army group
notes: Event date: 5 May 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 471-472: on the night of 4 May emissaries of Army Group G approached troops of the 3d Division of the XV Corps; the division commander, General O'Daniel, accompanied the delegation to an estate at Haar, near Munich, where negotiations began on the rainy fifth day of May; at about 1430 both sides signed the terms, effective at noon on 6 May). Event definition: the surrender of Army Group G to the 6th Army Group; the division escorts the delegation; the row is the place of the signing, not the division's own position. Relationship: XV Corps unspecified_subordination (from 28 Apr 45 to 5 May 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 12 Mar 45, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 15 Sep 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Haar, near Munich, where the signing took place on an estate (the estate is not named in the passage). Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Haar, Bavaria. Event support: moderate (one Green Book chapter, two pages). Location support: moderate (named town; the estate is not named).
